title: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) measures how concentrated the hemoglobin is in your red blood cells. It is one of the red blood cell indices reported as part of a complete blood count.
context: MCHC is used along with other red blood cell indices and blood tests to help tell apart different types of anemia. One index alone is not enough to make a diagnosis.
aboveRange: Can be associated with hemolytic anemia, when red blood cells are broken down faster than they can be replaced
Can be associated with hereditary spherocytosis, a rare genetic disorder
belowRange: Can be associated with iron deficiency anemia
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
